en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the social injustices and abuses of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and rarest eagles in the world.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao by indigenous ancestors over two thousand years ago.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution divides the national government into three co-equal branches: the executive, legislative, and judicial branches.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a vibrant, rhythmic two-step forward dance.
The Lumad is a collective term used to describe the diverse indigenous non-Muslim ethnic groups living in Mindanao.
Filipino scientist Dr. Ramon Barba invented a flower induction technology that allows mango trees to bear fruit year-round.
Baybayin was the ancient pre-colonial writing system used by early Filipinos before the arrival of Spanish colonizers.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument in Caloocan City to honor Andres Bonifacio and the Katipuneros.
The eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is traditionally shown when neighbors unite to carry a whole nipa hut to a new location.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site known for its rich marine biodiversity.
